title: The approval panel identifies the pending approver as a truncated raw id — `positi…ager` — so nobody can tell who is holding the record
body:
The approval panel identifies the pending approver as a truncated raw id — `positi…ager` — so nobody can tell who is holding the record

Measured on `17.1.0` (open edition, `objectstack dev`), HotCRM opportunity with a pending `approval` node.

## What the record page shows

```
审批
Large Deal Approval (on create) · Sales Manager Review
待审批
  1  Sales Manager Review
  2  Sales Director Sign-off
等待以下审批人
  positi…ager        ← the approver
  [催办]
```

`positi…ager` is `position:sales_manager` middle-truncated to fit its chip. The step names are human prose; the one line that answers *who is this waiting on* is an internal identifier, and not even a complete one.

The same string appears un-truncated in the admin-override dialog, which is otherwise a model of clarity:

```
你在该步骤没有审批人席位。继续将使用管理员越权:该步骤会立即结案,
并跳过尚未表态的审批人 —— position:sales_manager。
此决定将记录为管理员越权。
```

So the dialog explains a subtle governance concept in plain Chinese and then names the party as `position:sales_manager`.

## Expected

Resolve the approver reference to its display name before rendering — a position's label (`Sales Manager` / `销售经理`), and where the seat resolves to people, the people (`销售经理 · 张伟、李娜`). The raw `position:<name>` id is the right thing to show on hover or in a debug view, not as the primary identification.

If the seat cannot be resolved (unstaffed position — a real state, and one worth surfacing), say that: `销售经理（暂无在岗人员）` is actionable, `positi…ager` is not. As it stands a submitter chasing an approval has no name to chase, and the 催办 button next to it sends a reminder to a party the sender cannot see.

## Related

The same panel renders correctly in every other respect — step order, current step, decision history with attribution (`通过 · Dev Admin 管理员越权 · Manager Review`) and the override comment. It is specifically the approver identity that is unresolved.
